candidate.educational_objective: Differentiate H2-receptor antagonists from PPIs by their distinct targets in gastric acid secretion.

options.A: Both drug classes inhibit the same gastric receptor and differ only in onset time.
options.B: H2-receptor antagonists block histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells, whereas PPIs inhibit the gastric H+/K+ ATPase proton pump.
options.C: H2-receptor antagonists inhibit the gastric proton pump, whereas PPIs block histamine H2 receptors.
options.D: PPIs reduce acid secretion by blocking histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells.

candidate.rationale: H2-receptor antagonists decrease gastric acid secretion by competitively blocking histamine H2 receptors on gastric parietal cells. PPIs act at a different target: the parietal-cell H+/K+ ATPase, the final proton pump in gastric acid secretion. Therefore, B is correct.
